utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-99-36-A, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I please have appearances for the parties? First the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Katharina Margetts for the Prosecution with Senior Appeals Counsel Mark McKeon, and case manager, Andres Vatter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Margetts. The Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm John Ackerman along with Aleksandar Vujic for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. Mr. Brdjanin, can you hear me and can you understand me in the language you understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes, I do hear you and I understand you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin. You may be seated. This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was held on 9 November 2005. Almost 120 days have now passed since that Status Conference. I would like now, I would want to turn to Mr. Brdjanin and to ask you, Mr. Brdjanin, whether you have any issues that you would like to raise at this time, and whether you have any concerns about your physical or mental well-being. Mr. Brdjanin? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] At this time, there is nothing I have to raise. As far as my health is concerned, it is all very well. And, of course, any other concerns I may have, they are quite known to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin. I'm glad that you are well and you may be seated. The parties' submissions on their respective appeals from the trial judgement are now complete. There is only one outstanding motion in this case. The Defence motion to present Rule 115 evidence. This motion will be decided shortly. The Appeals Chamber hopes that fairly soon it will be able to schedule oral arguments on the merits of the appeals. Before concluding the Status Conference, I would now want to ask the counsel for the Prosecution and the Defence whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is nothing to raise from the Prosecution side. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We have nothing, Your Honour. Thank you very much. 7

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. As there are no other issues, I thank the parties for their attendance and call these proceedings to a close. Thank you very much.
